messages:
alex-infra: FYI - us-central GPU pool ejected 2 hosts due to OOM around 08:12 UTC. Autoscaler is trying to replace but quota/provisioning limits are blocking. Shedding low-priority traffic now to protect latency SLOs :warning:
maria-ml: any idea what triggered the OOM? model size spike or a bad batch?
alex-infra: early signs point to a high-concurrency tail from a customer running long-context evals. KV cache growth pushed memory. node logs show repeated OOM killer invoking nvidia-smi out-of-memory.
samir-eng: can we flip the load-shedding policy to token-priority instead of route-based? that should preserve interactive calls and drop bulk embedding jobs.
leo-sre: we can, but need a quick config change on the routing layer. patch available: `routes/priority_v2.yaml` — i can deploy canary in 2 mins.
emily-cs: heads up for CS — a handful of enterprise customers are seeing degraded throughput. We should post a status update and flag high-usage customers for manual escalation.
alex-infra: agreed. Proposed statuspage copy: "Degraded capacity in us-central causing increased latency and limited throughput for some workloads. We are shedding lower-priority requests while replacing ejected hosts. ETA for recovery ~45 minutes; will update if that changes." Thoughts?
maria-ml: fine but add a note about workaround: customers can pin to a different region (us-east1 or eu-west1) for full capacity.
emily-cs: please add: "If you rely on long-context batch evals, contact support and we can assist with temporary routing to other regions or a higher-priority queue." I'll start outbound pings to the 6 affected accounts.
samir-eng: deploying token-priority change now. command: ```kubectl apply -f routes/priority_v2.yaml --namespace=ingress```. rolling canary to 10% of traffic.
ops-bot: deploy started by samir-eng at 08:25 UTC — canary 10% -> 100% in 5m if no regressions.
leo-sre: canary looks good. token-priority active on canary nodes, no increase in error rates. advancing to 50%.
alex-infra: autoscaler still throttled by cloud quota — opened request to cloud-ops to increase instance quota (case 123456). ETA from cloud team currently 90m; will push for priority.
emily-cs: updating statuspage now with the copy and note about ETA 45 -> 90 minutes if quotas delayed. drafting DM for affected customers.
maria-ml: quick perf note — token-priority reduces throughput for batch jobs by ~60% but keeps tail latency for interactive under SLO. good trade.
alex-infra: statuspage update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1985012345 (Drafted message: "Degraded capacity in us-central... ETA 45m; could extend to 90m while cloud quota is provisioned.").
emily-cs: posted. also creating support tickets for the 6 accounts and tagging with priority:high.
samir-eng: autoscaler workaround: temporarily increase per-node pod eviction thresholds to avoid immediate ejection; applying patch in 2 minutes. note: this is riskier but buys time for quota.
leo-sre: wary of masking underlying memory issue. monitor OOM events closely. set alert on `node.oom.count` > 3/min.
ops-bot: alert rule `node.oom.count` created by leo-sre at 08:40 UTC.
alex-infra: update: cloud-ops acknowledged case, prioritizing. new ETA 60m. pushing to 45m.
emily-cs: will reflect new ETA in status and tell customers ETA 60m for now.
samir-eng: rolling back pod eviction threshold change after quota confirmed; switching to autoscaler-driven recovery.
alex-infra: final update for now: we've activated token-priority shedding, posted status update, notified affected customers, and opened quota escalation. Recovery ETA 60m. will post final when hosts return. :white_check_mark:"
